name: Gilt market
summary: 10-year gilt yield eased to 5.24% and 30-year to 5.72% on 20 Nov; long yields stay near multi-decade highs
state: The 10-year gilt yield rose above 5.35% on 16 Nov, its highest since 23 Oct, then fell to about 5.24% by 20 Nov after softer October inflation on 18 Nov and an equity sell-off that drove demand for bonds (Trading Economics). The 30-year yield closed near 5.72% on 20 Nov, about 7bp lower over the month but still close to levels last seen in 1998 (Trading Economics). The 10-year's monthly move is inside the 40bp line; Watch is kept because long yields remain near multi-decade highs, with no weak auction or BoE intervention found.
for_you: Gilt yields feed into fixed mortgage pricing and government borrowing costs. Markets still expect a further Bank Rate rise in December, which tends to keep new mortgage rates elevated.
rubric_hit: 30y gilt 5.72% near multi-decade highs: Watch; 10y monthly move < 40bp, no BoE intervention

sources.title: Trading Economics — UK Gilt Yields Surge as Rate Hike Expectations Mount

why: Gilt yields set UK mortgage rates and the government's borrowing costs; the 2022 LDI crisis showed how fast it can break.
drivers: Fiscal credibility, BoE policy, inflation, global bond moves, pension-fund flows.

rubric.alert: BoE intervention, or 10y moved > 75bp in a month.
rubric.watch: 30y gilt at multi-decade highs, or 10y moved 40–75bp in a month, or a weak auction.
rubric.normal: 10y gilt moved < 40bp in a month and auctions orderly.
